title: 2001-19 — Appeal TE Sung Keon Kim vs. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the appeal from the Judicial Commission’s finding of guilt and deposition, holding that BCO 32 and 34 procedures were not followed, and remanded to Presbytery for a new trial. It did not pass on the adequacy of the citations or comment on the merits.
first_summary: A minister appealed his deposition after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission found him guilty of participating in an unconstitutional presbytery meeting and of contumacy. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed the deposition, and remanded for a new trial because the commission had not followed BCO procedures. It did not reach the merits.
summary: On appeal from a minister’s deposition in a conflicted Korean Capital Presbytery church, the SJC asked whether the commission followed BCO procedures in instituting and conducting judicial process. It sustained the appeal, holding that no indictment appears to have been served and the record lacked minutes showing a trial, contrary to BCO 32-3’s writing, indictment, and service requirements. The SJC remanded to Presbytery for a new trial under BCO 32 and 34. It expressly did not rule on the adequacy of the citations or the merits.
